questions.q: Mr Bello's poultry farm in Ogbomoso has chickens that excrete a white, pasty material in their droppings. The nitrogenous waste that forms most of this material is
questions.explanation: Birds convert toxic ammonia into uric acid, which is only slightly soluble in water and is excreted as a semi-solid paste, helping them conserve water. Urea is the main nitrogenous waste of many mammals, while ammonia is usually excreted by many aquatic animals.

questions.q: Ngozi in Aba has just eaten a meal containing groundnuts and palm oil. Most of the digested fatty acids and glycerol are absorbed into the
questions.explanation: Fatty acids and glycerol are absorbed into the lacteals, which are lymphatic vessels in the villi, and are later transported by lymph. Water-soluble nutrients such as glucose and amino acids mostly enter the blood capillaries of the villi.

questions.q: A child named Musa in Maiduguri has soft, deformed bones and bow legs. His diet is most likely deficient in
questions.explanation: Vitamin D is needed for the absorption of calcium and phosphate and for proper bone formation, so its deficiency causes rickets, with soft bones and bow legs. Vitamin A deficiency mainly affects vision, vitamin B₁ deficiency causes beri-beri, and vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy.

questions.q: A student in Obudu observes a plant with vascular tissues and spores produced on the underside of its leaves. The plant is classified with the
questions.explanation: Ferns are vascular plants that reproduce by spores, commonly formed in sporangia on the undersides of their leaves. Mosses lack true vascular tissue, while conifers and angiosperms reproduce by seeds.

questions.q: Mrs Okoro in Awka is in the early weeks of pregnancy. Which structure is the main source of progesterone that maintains the endometrium before the placenta takes over?
questions.explanation: After ovulation, the corpus luteum secretes progesterone to maintain the thickened endometrium in early pregnancy. The placenta later becomes the main source of progesterone, while a Graafian follicle develops before ovulation and the anterior pituitary secretes gonadotrophins.

questions.q: A banana farmer in Akure has a variety that does not produce viable seeds. Which method is most suitable for reproducing the banana plants?
options: planting pieces of the fruit in moist soil
planting the suckers produced at the base of the parent plant
sowing the seeds after soaking them in water
questions.explanation: Bananas are commonly propagated vegetatively by planting suckers or corms, producing genetically identical offspring without the need for viable seeds. Hand pollination would not work if viable seeds are not formed, and pieces of fruit do not develop into new banana plants.

questions.q: A biology student in Ilorin reads that new alleles arise in a species from time to time. Which process is the ultimate source of such new alleles?
questions.explanation: Mutation changes the DNA base sequence and can produce a new allele, so it is the ultimate source of new genetic variation. Natural selection and genetic drift change allele frequencies, while sexual reproduction reshuffles existing alleles.

questions.q: Two populations of the same grasshopper species live on opposite banks of a wide river. After many generations, they are brought together and no longer produce fertile offspring. This outcome is best described as
questions.explanation: The populations have become reproductively isolated and can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring, which is the formation of new species. Competition and succession are ecological processes, while mutation is a source of variation rather than the final outcome described.

questions.q: In aerobic respiration, which stage produces the greatest amount of ATP per glucose molecule?
options: Conversion of pyruvic acid to lactic acid
questions.explanation: Most ATP is made during oxidative phosphorylation as electrons pass along the electron transport chain and drive ATP synthesis. Glycolysis and the Krebs cycle produce some ATP, while conversion of pyruvic acid to lactic acid is anaerobic and yields no extra ATP.

questions.q: During vigorous exercise, a student in Abuja finds that his muscles respire anaerobically for a short time. What happens to pyruvic acid under these conditions?
options: It is completely broken down to carbon dioxide and water.
It is converted to lactic acid.
It is stored directly as glycogen in the muscle.
It is converted to ethanol and carbon dioxide.
questions.explanation: When oxygen is insufficient, human muscle cells convert pyruvic acid to lactic acid, allowing glycolysis to continue by regenerating NAD⁺. Complete breakdown to carbon dioxide and water requires oxygen, while ethanol and carbon dioxide are formed in yeast, not human muscle.

questions.q: In a pond near Makurdi, the food chain is algae → mosquito larvae → small fish → kingfisher. Which term best describes the small fish in this food chain?
questions.explanation: Mosquito larvae feed on algae and are primary consumers; small fish then feed on the larvae, making them secondary consumers. Producers make their own food, while decomposers break down dead organic matter.

questions.q: A biology class in Ogun State studies a population of grasshoppers on a patch of grassland. The population grows until it levels off because food and space become limited. What name is given to the maximum population size the habitat can support?
questions.explanation: Carrying capacity is the maximum number of individuals of a species that an environment can support over time. Population density is the number per unit area, an ecological niche is the organism's role, and a limiting factor is a condition that restricts growth.

questions.q: In a swamp near Calabar, water lilies, algae, tadpoles, small fish and crabs live together and interact. Which term describes all the populations of these organisms living together in the area?
questions.explanation: A community consists of all the different populations living and interacting in a given area. An ecosystem includes the community plus the physical environment, while a population is made up of members of one species.

questions.q: A test cross is carried out by crossing an organism showing a dominant trait with a homozygous recessive organism. What is the main purpose of this cross?
options: To make all the offspring show the recessive trait
To find out whether the dominant-looking parent is homozygous or heterozygous
To produce a pure-breeding line immediately
To increase the rate of mutation in the offspring
questions.explanation: If the dominant-looking parent is homozygous, all offspring show the dominant trait; if it is heterozygous, about half show the recessive trait. The test cross therefore reveals the unknown genotype. It does not increase mutation or directly create pure lines.

questions.q: Why are recessive sex-linked disorders generally more common in males than in females?
options: Males have two X chromosomes, so recessive alleles are expressed more easily.
Females have only one X chromosome and cannot carry the allele.
Males have only one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele on the X is expressed.
The alleles are always carried on the Y chromosome and affect only males.
questions.explanation: A male has one X and one Y chromosome, so a recessive allele on his single X chromosome has no matching allele on the Y to mask it. A female has two X chromosomes, so she usually needs two copies of the recessive allele to show the disorder.

questions.q: A 2-year-old child in Abeokuta is brought to a clinic with fever and sudden weakness of both legs. A stool sample is sent to test for a virus that attacks motor neurones. Which disease is most likely being investigated?
questions.explanation: Poliomyelitis is caused by poliovirus, which attacks motor neurones and can lead to paralysis; the virus may also be found in stool. Malaria and tuberculosis do not fit this nervous-system picture, while tetanus is caused by a bacterial toxin and is not detected by testing stool for a virus.

questions.q: A health worker in Kaduna finds that a child has a circular, scaly skin patch with broken hairs. Which type of microorganism causes this condition?
questions.explanation: The description is typical of ringworm, a skin infection caused by fungi. The circular scaly patch and broken hairs help distinguish it from many bacterial or viral skin infections, and protozoans do not cause this type of skin lesion.

questions.q: Which measure is most effective in reducing transmission of HIV from a pregnant woman to her baby in a Nigerian hospital?
options: Giving the mother and baby prescribed antiretroviral drugs
Isolating the mother from other patients
questions.explanation: Antiretroviral drugs lower the amount of HIV in the mother and protect the baby during pregnancy, birth and breastfeeding. HIV is not spread by ordinary hospital contact or mosquito bites, so isolation, measles vaccination and insecticide-treated nets do not prevent mother-to-child transmission.

questions.q: A man in Jos eats a meal containing a large amount of salt and later feels very thirsty. Which part of the brain responds to the increased solute concentration of the blood and stimulates thirst?
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus contains osmoreceptors that detect changes in blood solute concentration and stimulate thirst, as well as ADH release. The cerebellum coordinates balance, the medulla controls involuntary actions such as breathing, and the cerebrum is mainly involved in conscious thought and voluntary actions.

questions.q: A footballer in Kaduna continues to breathe faster and deeper after sprinting. Which part of the brain controls the rate and depth of breathing?
questions.explanation: The medulla oblongata contains the respiratory centre, which regulates the rate and depth of breathing unconsciously. The cerebellum coordinates balance and muscular movement, the cerebrum controls voluntary activity, and the hypothalamus regulates temperature, thirst and hormone-related functions.

questions.q: A boy in Bauchi has a small cut on his knee, and bleeding stops after a few minutes. Which blood component releases substances that initiate the clotting process when a blood vessel is damaged?
questions.explanation: Platelets release substances that start the clotting reactions, leading to the formation of a fibrin network that seals the wound. Red blood cells carry oxygen, white blood cells defend the body, and plasma is the liquid part of blood rather than the component that initiates clotting.

questions.q: In the kidney, glucose is reabsorbed from the filtrate into the blood even when its concentration in the filtrate becomes lower than in the blood. Which process makes this possible?
questions.explanation: Active transport uses energy and carrier proteins to move glucose against its concentration gradient from the filtrate into the blood. Diffusion would only move glucose down its concentration gradient, osmosis concerns water movement, and pressure filtration is involved in forming the filtrate rather than reabsorbing glucose.

questions.q: A grasshopper is found to shed its exoskeleton several times before reaching the adult stage. The shedding is necessary mainly because the exoskeleton
options: is rigid and cannot expand continually as the insect grows
contains living cells that must be replaced regularly
offers no protection until the adult stage
is made of calcium carbonate that dissolves in body fluid
questions.explanation: The exoskeleton is a rigid covering of chitin. It cannot stretch indefinitely, so it must be shed periodically to allow increase in body size before a new covering hardens. It is protective at all stages and is not dissolved by body fluid.

questions.q: A biology student in Abeokuta observes an earthworm moving through moist soil. The body is supported by pressure of fluid in the coelom against the body wall. This type of skeleton is best described as
questions.explanation: Fluid under pressure in the coelom supports the earthworm and provides resistance against which muscles act. An exoskeleton is an external hardened covering, while an endoskeleton is internal and usually jointed.

questions.q: When a person in Enugu bends the forearm to lift a bucket, the biceps contracts while the triceps relaxes. Why is this arrangement of muscles important at the elbow?
options: It enables the forearm to rotate freely in all planes.
It allows one muscle to pull the forearm in one direction while the other pulls it in the opposite direction.
It permits each muscle to push the bone back after pulling it.
It allows both muscles to contract strongly at the same time.
questions.explanation: The biceps and triceps are antagonistic muscles; when one contracts, the other relaxes, so the forearm can be raised or lowered. Skeletal muscles can only pull, not push, and the elbow is a hinge joint that mainly allows movement in one plane.

questions.q: A root hair cell of an onion plant absorbs mineral salts from the soil against a concentration gradient. Which organelle is most directly responsible for providing the energy required for this process?
questions.explanation: Active uptake of mineral salts requires energy in the form of ATP, which is produced mainly by mitochondria during respiration. Chloroplasts are not present in root hair cells, while the vacuole and cell wall do not supply ATP for active transport.

questions.q: A student in Calabar observes a cell with numerous Golgi apparatuses and many vesicles being released at the cell surface. Which activity is most likely taking place in the cell?
options: Movement of chromosomes during cell division
Secretion of substances such as enzymes
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies, packages and transports materials in vesicles, especially for secretion. Hydrogen peroxide breakdown occurs in peroxisomes, starch formation in chloroplasts, and chromosome movement involves spindle fibres.

questions.q: A man in Maiduguri has not taken water for several hours on a hot afternoon. His pituitary gland releases more antidiuretic hormone. What effect will this hormone have on his kidney tubules?
options: It stops the reabsorption of glucose, causing glucose in urine.
It increases water reabsorption, producing a smaller volume of concentrated urine.
It increases water loss, producing a larger volume of dilute urine.
It increases the filtration of blood cells into the tubule.
questions.explanation: Antidiuretic hormone makes the collecting duct more permeable to water, so more water is reabsorbed into the blood. This reduces urine volume and makes the urine more concentrated. Blood cells are normally not filtered, and glucose is reabsorbed in a healthy person.

questions.q: The loop of Henle is much longer in a kangaroo rat living in a dry desert than in a beaver living near water. The longer loop is an adaptation for
options: filtering large plasma proteins from the blood
secreting more glucose into the filtrate
increasing the loss of salts in dilute urine
reabsorbing more water to produce highly concentrated urine
questions.explanation: A longer loop of Henle creates a steeper osmotic gradient in the medulla, allowing more water to be reabsorbed from the collecting duct. This helps the desert animal conserve water and excrete concentrated urine. Large plasma proteins are not normally filtered, and losing more salts in dilute urine would waste water.

questions.q: A patient in Ibadan has a blocked pancreatic duct, and undigested fat appears in the stools. Which enzyme deficiency most directly accounts for this observation?
questions.explanation: Pancreatic lipase breaks fats into fatty acids and glycerol, and its reduced supply allows fat to pass out undigested. Pepsin acts on proteins in the stomach, while maltase and sucrase act on specific sugars.

questions.q: A child in Sokoto eats mainly polished maize and develops pellagra, with dermatitis, diarrhoea and mental confusion. The diet is most likely deficient in
questions.explanation: Pellagra is caused by a deficiency of niacin, which is poorly available in a diet based mainly on polished maize. Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy, vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness, and vitamin D deficiency causes rickets.

questions.q: A student in Makurdi collects a slow-moving organism with a soft unsegmented body, a muscular foot and a mantle. To which phylum does it belong?
questions.explanation: A soft, unsegmented body with a muscular foot and a mantle is characteristic of the phylum Mollusca, which includes snails and slugs. Arthropoda have jointed appendages and an exoskeleton, while Annelida have segmented bodies and Echinodermata have spiny-skinned bodies with radial symmetry. The mantle and muscular foot rule out those other phyla.

questions.q: A biology teacher in Calabar explains that a whale is classified as a mammal even though it lives in water. Which feature best supports its classification as a mammal?
questions.explanation: Mammals are characterised by mammary glands, hair and a diaphragm; the whale possesses mammary glands and suckles its young. A streamlined body and gills are features of fish, while scales are not typical of mammals.

questions.q: A biology student in Ibadan is arranging organisms on a chart. Which sequence of taxonomic ranks is correct from the largest group to the smallest?
options: Species → Genus → Family → Order → Class → Phylum → Kingdom
Kingdom → Class → Phylum → Order → Family → Genus → Species
Kingdom → Phylum → Order → Class → Family → Genus → Species
Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species
questions.explanation: The standard hierarchy from largest to smallest is kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus and species. The other sequences interchange ranks such as phylum and class or order and class, or arrange them in the reverse direction. A species is the smallest rank in the list, so it should appear at the end when moving from largest to smallest.

questions.q: A woman in Enugu complains that she does not want another pregnancy soon and is advised to use a diaphragm. How does a diaphragm prevent pregnancy?
options: It covers the cervix and prevents sperm from reaching the uterus.
It prevents the uterus from preparing its lining.
It stops the ovary from releasing an ovum.
It kills all sperm cells by chemical action.
questions.explanation: A diaphragm is a barrier contraceptive placed over the cervix, so it blocks sperm from entering the uterus and meeting the ovum. It does not stop ovulation, kill sperm chemically, or alter the uterine lining. Those effects are associated with other contraceptive methods.

questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of sexual reproduction over asexual reproduction?
options: It allows a single parent to produce offspring.
It produces offspring with genetic variation.
It produces many identical offspring quickly.
questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction combines genetic material from two parents, so the offspring show genetic variation, which can help the species survive environmental changes. Producing offspring from a single parent without variation is a feature of asexual reproduction. Speed and identical offspring are also advantages of asexual reproduction, not sexual reproduction.

questions.q: Which of the following human characteristics is an example of discontinuous variation?
questions.explanation: Discontinuous variation places individuals into distinct categories with no intermediates, and ABO blood groups are clearly separate types. Body mass, height and skin colour normally vary continuously over a range. Therefore the blood group is the characteristic showing discontinuous variation.

questions.q: In parts of Nigeria where malaria is common, the sickle-cell trait is maintained in the population because people with the trait have some resistance to malaria. Which explanation best accounts for this?
options: Malaria causes new sickle-cell alleles to appear in each generation.
The sickle-cell allele is always beneficial to homozygous individuals.
Natural selection favours heterozygous individuals in malaria-prone areas.
People with normal haemoglobin are completely immune to malaria.
questions.explanation: In malaria-prone areas, individuals heterozygous for the sickle-cell allele survive better than those with normal haemoglobin because they have some resistance to malaria, while homozygous sickle-cell individuals are often severely affected. This heterozygote advantage keeps the allele at a relatively high frequency in the population. Malaria does not create new alleles; mutations are the source of new alleles.

questions.q: Which equation represents aerobic respiration in living cells?
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration uses glucose and oxygen to release energy, producing carbon dioxide and water as shown in the equation with glucose plus six oxygen molecules. The equation producing ethanol and carbon dioxide represents anaerobic respiration in yeast, and the equation using carbon dioxide and water as reactants with oxygen as a product represents photosynthesis. The equation with carbon dioxide as a reactant and oxygen as a product is not the correct aerobic respiration equation.

questions.q: Which feature prevents the trachea of a mammal from collapsing during breathing?
questions.explanation: The trachea is held open by incomplete C-shaped rings of cartilage, which support it while still allowing the oesophagus to expand during swallowing. Bone and chitin are not found in the tracheal wall, and smooth muscle does not provide the main rigid support that prevents collapse. This cartilage support keeps the airway open for air movement.

questions.q: In a pond near Epe, water fern spreads over the surface and shades the water below. The submerged plants in the pond begin to die mainly because they cannot obtain enough
questions.explanation: The water fern covers the pond surface and reduces the amount of light reaching the submerged plants. Without enough light, the submerged plants cannot carry out photosynthesis efficiently and eventually die.

questions.q: In a forest near Calabar, a fern grows on the branch of a large tree. It obtains sunlight and moisture from the air but does not take nutrients from the tree. The relationship between the fern and the tree is best described as
questions.explanation: The fern benefits by obtaining a suitable place to grow, while the tree is not harmed and does not benefit. This one-sided benefit without harm is commensalism.

questions.q: During a class discussion in Ibadan on global warming, a student states that carbon dioxide in the atmosphere is removed by a biological process. Which process removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere?
options: decay of dead matter by bacteria
questions.explanation: Green plants take in carbon dioxide and use it during photosynthesis to produce food. Respiration, decay and burning of fossil fuels release carbon dioxide rather than remove it from the atmosphere.

questions.q: A sample of DNA from a cowpea plant near Ilorin contains 30% adenine. What percentage of its bases is cytosine?
questions.explanation: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine, so thymine is also 30%. Adenine and thymine together make 60%, leaving 40% for guanine and cytosine; since guanine equals cytosine, cytosine is 20%.

questions.q: A community health officer in Ibadan advises residents to drain stagnant water from discarded containers. Which stage in the life cycle of the malaria mosquito is most directly controlled by this measure?
options: entry of sporozoites into liver cells
formation of gametes in the human host
development of mosquito larvae in water
questions.explanation: Mosquitoes lay eggs in stagnant water, and their larvae develop there. Draining the water removes the breeding sites and directly prevents larval development, reducing the number of adult mosquitoes.

questions.q: A nurse in Owerri wants to protect newborn babies in the community from tetanus. Which measure is most effective?
options: giving all newborn babies antibiotics after birth
immunising pregnant women with tetanus toxoid
isolating newborn babies from other children
questions.explanation: Tetanus toxoid given to a pregnant woman stimulates her body to produce antibodies. These antibodies pass to the fetus and protect the newborn baby against tetanus.

questions.q: During a hot afternoon in Maiduguri, a student sweats and his skin blood vessels widen, helping to keep body temperature steady. Which part of the brain controls these responses?
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus acts as the body's thermoregulatory centre. It detects changes in blood temperature and triggers responses such as sweating and widening of skin blood vessels.

questions.q: After eating a large plate of pounded yam in Aba, a person's blood glucose rises. Which hormone is secreted to lower the blood glucose back to normal?
questions.explanation: Insulin is secreted by the pancreas when blood glucose is high. It increases glucose uptake by cells and promotes the conversion of glucose to glycogen in the liver, lowering blood glucose.

questions.q: A 5.0 cm strip of cocoyam was placed in 0.5 mol dm⁻³ sucrose solution. After 30 minutes, its length was 4.6 cm. What is the percentage decrease in length?
questions.explanation: The length decreased by 5.0 cm − 4.6 cm = 0.4 cm. The percentage decrease is (0.4 ÷ 5.0) × 100% = 8%.

questions.q: In an experiment in Zaria, root hairs of a maize seedling absorbed nitrate ions from a culture solution even when the nitrate concentration in the solution was lower than that inside the root hair cells. When a metabolic poison was added, nitrate uptake stopped. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Nitrate uptake is due to diffusion from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration
Nitrate uptake occurs by osmosis because water is also absorbed
The poison increased the permeability of the root hair membrane to nitrate ions
Nitrate uptake uses energy from respiration and is an active process
questions.explanation: The ions were taken up against a concentration gradient, and uptake stopped when metabolism was poisoned. This shows that the process requires energy from respiration, which is characteristic of active transport.

questions.q: Which feature best adapts an artery to the high pressure of blood leaving the heart?
options: Valves at intervals along its length to prevent backflow
One-way valves and a thin endothelial wall
A thick wall containing elastic tissue and smooth muscle
A very wide lumen and thin muscular wall
questions.explanation: Arteries receive blood at high pressure, so their thick elastic and muscular walls help them withstand and smooth the pressure surges. Valves are characteristic of veins, while a wide lumen with a thin wall is more typical of veins.

questions.q: A student in Abeokuta examined a transverse section of a young dicot stem. Which tissue is mainly responsible for transporting water and dissolved mineral salts upward?
options: Phloem sieve tubes and companion cells
questions.explanation: Xylem vessels and tracheids are dead, hollow conducting cells that carry water and mineral salts upward from the roots. Phloem mainly transports organic solutes, cambium produces new cells, and pith is primarily for storage.

questions.q: During vigorous exercise in Abuja, a man's skeletal muscles require more oxygen. Which change in his circulatory system most directly increases oxygen delivery to the muscles?
options: The heart rate decreases so that blood spends longer in the lungs
Arterioles supplying the muscles constrict and blood is diverted to the skin
Arterioles supplying the muscles dilate and blood flow through the muscles increases
The number of red blood cells in the blood increases immediately
questions.explanation: During exercise, local arterioles in active muscles dilate, increasing blood flow and therefore oxygen delivery. Constriction would reduce flow, and the red blood cell count does not rise immediately during exercise.

questions.q: A footballer in Lagos injures a tough band of connective tissue that joins the tibia to the femur at the knee. Which structure has been injured?
questions.explanation: A ligament is a strong band that joins one bone to another, such as the tibia to the femur at the knee. A tendon joins muscle to bone, while cartilage and the synovial membrane are not the main bone-to-bone binding structures.

questions.q: A student in Benin compared a young herbaceous stem with a woody stem of a mature plant. Which feature gives the woody stem greater rigidity?
options: A waxy cuticle on the epidermis
questions.explanation: Lignin strengthens the walls of xylem cells and gives woody tissue its rigidity. Turgid parenchyma supports young herbaceous stems but is not the main source of rigidity in mature woody stems.

questions.q: A scientist in Ibadan treats a living cell with a chemical that destroys its ribosomes. Which cell activity is most directly stopped?
options: Movement of water across the cell membrane
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis, so destroying them directly stops protein production. ATP production occurs mainly in mitochondria, starch storage involves plastids, and water movement across the membrane is mainly by osmosis.

questions.q: A biology student in Nsukka cuts through a fresh mammalian kidney. In which part are the glomeruli mainly located?
questions.explanation: The glomeruli are found in the renal cortex, where filtration of blood begins. The renal medulla contains mainly loops of Henle and collecting ducts, while the pelvis collects urine before it enters the ureter.

questions.q: Which process takes place in the glomerulus of a mammalian kidney?
options: Ultrafiltration of small molecules from blood plasma
Reabsorption of most water under ADH control
questions.explanation: The glomerulus filters small molecules such as water, glucose and urea from blood plasma into Bowman's capsule. Selective reabsorption occurs later in the tubule, while urea is formed from ammonia in the liver.

questions.q: A health worker in Enugu advises a pregnant woman to eat green leafy vegetables such as spinach because they supply a vitamin needed for normal blood clotting. Which vitamin is this?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is required for the formation of clotting factors such as prothrombin in the liver. Vitamin A is mainly needed for vision, vitamin C for collagen formation and immunity, and vitamin D for calcium absorption.

questions.q: A pregnant woman in Aba is told that nutrients and oxygen pass from her blood to the fetus. Through which structure does this exchange mainly occur?
questions.explanation: The placenta is the organ where maternal and fetal blood come close enough for exchange of nutrients, oxygen and waste products. The umbilical cord carries fetal blood to and from the placenta, while the amnion protects the fetus with fluid.
